back: Fixed schema of rows and identical typed columns — the shape of relational tables, queryable with SQL.
Carries labelled fields that can vary record to record — JSON, XML, key-value. Schema travels with the data.
No queryable schema: images, audio, video, free documents. Lives in object storage like Azure Blob.
Columnar file formats — values grouped by column, so analytical scans of a few columns are fast and small. Row formats (CSV, Avro) suit transactions and streams.
Many small current reads/writes recording business events, protected by ACID guarantees.
Fewer, heavier queries scanning large volumes of history for trends and aggregates — kept in stores separate from live OLTP systems.
Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability — the transaction guarantees of OLTP databases.
Availability, backup and restore, performance tuning, and user access on databases.
Builds and operates ingestion and transformation pipelines that land data where analysts can use it.
Explores and models data, builds visualizations and reports — the Power BI seat.
Primary key uniquely identifies each row; a foreign key in another table references it, forming the relationship.
Splitting data into related tables so each fact is stored once — prevents update anomalies, at the cost of joins.
DML works on rows: SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE. DDL works on objects: CREATE, ALTER, DROP.
A saved query presented as a virtual table — write the join once, SELECT from it forever.
Executable logic kept inside the database, invoked by name.
A lookup structure on chosen columns that lets the engine seek rows instead of scanning the whole table.
Fully managed, database-scoped PaaS — least administration; the default for new cloud apps.
PaaS with near-full instance-scoped SQL Server compatibility — SQL Agent and cross-database queries survive the migration.
IaaS: the full product on an OS you control — maximum compatibility for lift-and-shift, you patch and back up.
Managed PaaS versions of the open-source engines — same skills and drivers, Azure runs the servers.
Object storage for unstructured data at massive scale, with hot/cool/archive access tiers.
Managed SMB file shares that apps mount like a network drive — the lift-and-shift answer for file-path apps.
Simple, cheap NoSQL key-value store addressed by partition key + row key. No joins or rich queries.
Globally distributed multi-model NoSQL: millisecond latency, elastic scale, turnkey multi-region replication.
NoSQL (JSON documents), MongoDB, Apache Cassandra (wide-column), Apache Gremlin (graph), Table — match the API to the app's existing data model.

front: When Cosmos DB over Table storage?
back: When you need global distribution, guaranteed low latency, rich queries, or multiple data models — Table storage is the simple, cheap keyed store.
ETL transforms before loading into the destination; ELT lands raw data and transforms inside the analytical store.
Curated, structured, query-ready data modelled for fast SQL reporting.
Vast raw files in open formats, structure deferred until use.
Warehouse-style tables and governance layered over lake storage — one copy of data serving both engineering and SQL analytics.
The Apache Spark-based analytics platform for large-scale data engineering and data science.
Unified analytics SaaS — lakehouses, warehouses, pipelines, real-time intelligence, and Power BI over one data foundation, OneLake.
Batch: gather and process on a schedule, high latency, huge throughput. Streaming: process events as they arrive, insight in seconds.
Event Hubs ingests millions of events per second; Stream Analytics runs continuous queries over those streams.
Desktop authors models and reports; the service publishes, shares, refreshes, and serves dashboards (plus mobile apps to view).
A calculation defined in the data model — totals, ratios — so every report computes it consistently.
Trend over time → line. Compare categories → bar/column. Part of whole → pie (sparingly). Two measures → scatter. Geography → map. One number → card/KPI.
